nodes.name: NF cleaning
nodes.procedure: Firstly, NF was ultrasonically cleaned in CH3COCH3, HCl, and DI water for 30 min to dispose surface impurities.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, NF was ultrasonically cleaned in CH3COCH3, HCl, and DI water for 30 min to dispose surface impurities.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Co precursor growth
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol of CoCl2·6H2O was dissolved into 30 mL DI water and stirred for 10 min, then 2 mmol of CO(NH2)2 was added to the above solution to form a homogeneous aqueous solution under stirred for 10 min. Next, 3 mmol of NH4F was added to the mixture and stirred for another 10 min to obtain a transparent solution. Subsequently, a piece of NF (1×2 cm²) was put into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave, the above solution was also poured into autoclave, and heated at 120°C for 15 h. Finally, the obtained product was taken out, and washed for further use, and denoted as Co-P@NF.

nodes.source_text: The cobalt precursor (CoP) nanoflowers was grown on NF (Co-P@NF) through a simple hydrothermal process... heated at 120°C for 15 h.

nodes.name: Calcination to Co3O4
nodes.procedure: The as-synthesized Co-P@NF was annealed at 300°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ in air atmosphere, and denoted as Co3O4@NF.
nodes.source_text: The as-synthesized Co-P@NF was annealed at 300°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ in air atmosphere, and denoted as Co3O4@NF.

nodes.name: Oxygen vacancy etching
nodes.procedure: The Co3O4@NF was soaked in 50 mL of 0.2M NaBH4 solution at 25°C for 10 min, then washed for further use, and denoted as Vo-Co3O4@NF.
nodes.source_text: The Co3O4 with oxygen vacancies on NF was obtained by soaking the above Co3O4@NF in 50 mL of 0.2M NaBH4 solution at 25°C for 10 min.

nodes.name: Sulfuration to Co3S4
nodes.procedure: The as-synthesized Co-P@NF was immersed in 30 mL 0.2M Na2S solution and hydrothermally treated at 160°C for 15 h. Then, the obtained product was taken out, washed for further use, and denoted as Co3S4@NF.
nodes.source_text: The as-synthesized Co-P@NF was immersed in 30 mL 0.2M Na2S solution and hydrothermally treated at 160°C for 15 h.

nodes.name: Sulfur vacancy etching
nodes.procedure: The Co3S4@NF was soaked in 50 mL of 0.2M NaBH4 solution at 25°C for 10 min, then washed for further use, and denoted as Vs-Co3S4@NF.
nodes.source_text: The Co3S4 with sulfur vacancies on NF was obtained by soaking the above Co3S4@NF in 50 mL of 0.2M NaBH4 solution at 25°C for 10 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images (Fig. 1a,e,i,m) show all four catalysts maintain nanoflower morphology on NF; V₀-Co₃O₄@NF has rough nanoneedle surface, Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows large sparse porous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1a... Fig. 1i... Fig. 1e... Fig. 1m...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images (Fig. 1b,f,j,n) confirm nanoneedle structures; V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows porous nanoparticles, Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows larger voids accelerating electrolyte ingress.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of Co₃O₄@NF... Fig. 1f... Fig. 1j... Fig. 1n...

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of Co₃O₄@NF shows interplanar spacing of 0.465 nm corresponding to (111) plane of spinel Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of the Co₃O₄@NF displays that the interplanar spacing of 0.465 nm is consistent with the spacing of the (111) plane...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of Co₃O₄@NF shows diffraction rings of (220), (400) and (422) planes confirming spinel Co₃O₄ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the Co₃O₄@NF also exhibits clear diffraction rings of the (220), (400) and (422) plane...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows wrinkled nanoneedles become porous structures composed of closely connected nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be obviously observed in the TEM image (Fig. 1f), the wrinkled nanoneedles actually become porous structures and are composed of closely connected nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows (111) lattice plane of Co₃O₄ with disorganized lattice fringes indicating defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image (Fig. 1g) also presents lattice fringes corresponding to the (111) lattice plane of Co₃O₄, while the disorganized lattice fringe reveals the existence of defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows diffraction spots of (220), (311), and (422) matching Co₃O₄ crystal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the SAED pattern (Fig. 1h) manifests diffraction spots of (220), (311), and (422), which are matched well with the Co₃O₄ crystal.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of Co₃S₄@NF shows interplanar spacing of 0.285 nm consistent with (311) plane of spinel Co₃S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1k exhibits that the interplanar spacing of 0.285 nm of Co₃S₄@NF is consistent with the spacing of the (311) plane of the spinel Co₃S₄ crystal.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of Co₃S₄@NF displays diffraction rings of (311), (400), and (440) planes of Co₃S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SAED pattern (Fig. 1l) displays diffraction rings attributing to (311), (400), and (440) planes of Co₃S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows many dislocations indicating defect-rich structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Many dislocations are observed in Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF nanoflowers, as labeled by the red circle circles in Fig. 1o, which suggests the existence of defect-rich structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF exhibits diffraction of (400), (511), and (620) crystal planes of Co₃S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEAD image of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF in Fig. 1p exhibits the diffraction of the (400), (511), and (620) crystal planes of the Co₃S₄...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Co₃O₄@NF shows peaks at 2θ = 19.01°, 31.25°, 36.89°, 59.36°, 65.24° corresponding to (111), (220), (311), (511), (440) of spinel Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As denoted in Fig. 2a, except the diffraction peak of NF, all the other peaks at 2θ of 19.01°, 31.25°, 36.89°, 59.36°, 65.24° are originated from the (111), (220), (311), (511), and (440) reflections...
After vulcanization... new diffraction peaks at 2θ of 16.11°, 26.71°, 31.42°, 38.05°, 47.29°, 50.23°, and 55.01°, corresponding to the (111), (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), and (440) planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows disappeared peaks at 26.67° and 50.23° indicating sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison with Co₃S₄@NF, the diffraction peaks of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF at 26.67° and 50.23° are disappeared, which can be classified as the existence of sulfur vacancies...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of Co₃O₄@NF and V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows F₂g, E_g, A₁g peaks; V₀-Co₃O₄@NF main peak at 660 cm⁻¹ shows blue-shift and broadening due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum... display the same vibration peaks including F₂g, E_g, and A₁g... Compared to the Co₃O₄@NF, the main peak of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF at 660 cm⁻¹ shows a distinct blue-shift and broadening...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of Co₃S₄@NF and Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows F₂g (133, 275, 316 cm⁻¹), E_g (250 cm⁻¹), A₁g (347 cm⁻¹); Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF peaks shift to lower wavenumbers due to sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, five characteristic peaks of F₂g (133, 275, and 316 cm⁻¹), E_g (250 cm⁻¹), A₁g (347 cm⁻¹)... The Raman peaks of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF displays a tendency to move to a lower direction...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows wide signal peak at g = 2.003 due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 2e, owing to the existence of oxygen vacancies in the lattice, a wide signal peak generates at g = 2.003.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows intensified and widened signal at g = 2.004 indicating more sulfur vacancies than oxygen vacancies in V₀-Co₃O₄@NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile... the signal appears at g = 2.004... compared with V₀-Co₃O₄@NF, the EPR signal peak of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF was apparently more intensified and widened...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O 1s of Co₃O₄@NF and V₀-Co₃O₄@NF shows three peaks for Co-O, O vacancies, O-OH; V₀-Co₃O₄@NF has higher peak at 531.2 eV indicating oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution O 1 s spectra... the three peaks are individually caused by Co-O bond (O_I), O vacancies (O_II) and O-O(H) (O_III)... higher peak near at 531.2 eV of V₀-Co₃O₄@NF...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Co 2p of Co₃O₄@NF shows Co²⁺ at 797.9, 782.6 eV and Co³⁺ at 796.3, 780.5 eV; V₀-Co₃O₄@NF has higher Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio indicating oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p spectra... peaks located at 797.9 and 782.6 eV are corresponded to Co²⁺... higher percentage of the ratio of Co²⁺/Co³⁺... in V₀-Co₃O₄@NF...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Co 2p of Co₃S₄@NF and Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows Co 2p₃/₂ at 778.6, 780.1 eV and Co 2p₁/₂ at 793.6, 796.6 eV; Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF has Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio of 2.91 indicating sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As clearly manifested in Fig. 3d, the peaks at near 778.6 and 780.1 eV, 793.6 and 796.6 eV... According to XPS-peak differentiation-imitating analysis (Table S2),... ratio of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ in Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF is 2.91...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS S 2p of Co₃S₄@NF and Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF shows peaks at 169.0 eV (sat.), 164.0 eV (Co-S), 162.6 eV (S²⁻ low coordination), 163.3/161.5 eV (S 2p); Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF S 2p₁/₂ area ratio increases from 0.06 to 0.14 indicating sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, five well-resolved peaks were detected in the S 2p XPS spectrum... the relative peak area ratio of S 2p₁/₂ was 0.06 for Co₃S₄@NF, and this ratio increased to 0.14 for Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region for OER shows C_dl values: Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF (52 mF·cm⁻²), Co₃S₄@NF (20 mF·cm⁻²), V₀-Co₃O₄@NF (34 mF·cm⁻²), Co₃O₄@NF (5 mF·cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4e, the C_dl value of catalysts were calculated according to their CV curves (Fig. S2). The C_dl value of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF is 52 mF·cm⁻²...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region for HER shows C_dl values: Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF (155 mF·cm⁻²), V₀-Co₃O₄@NF (23 mF·cm⁻²), Co₃S₄@NF (127 mF·cm⁻²), Co₃O₄@NF (18 mF·cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As clearly depicted in Fig. 5e, the C_dl value of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF, V₀-Co₃O₄@NF, Co₃S₄@NF, and Co₃O₄@NF were 155, 23, 127, and 18 mF·cm⁻² respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS for OER shows R_ct of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF = 0.7 Ω, lower than Co₃S₄@NF (2.46 Ω), V₀-Co₃O₄@NF (1.43 Ω), Co₃O₄@NF (7.16 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4d displays that the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) value of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF was 0.7 Ω, which is also much lower than that of Co₃S₄@NF (2.46 Ω)...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS for HER shows Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF has smallest R_ct indicating fastest charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 5d, according to Nyquist plots, the R_ct of Vₛ-Co₃S₄@NF is the smallest...
